description: The jabberwock defined ANALYSIS as the order-N operation above figure-detection: group the detected figures into threads by shared referent, sum their displacement vectors (trust-weighted) within each thread, align threads to find the principal trajectory + counter-current, and emit one trajectory Reading accounting for all figures, with coherence and tension scores.

microtheory.name: text_analysis
microtheory.description: order-N analysis of a whole passage

attrs.name: analysis
attrs.description: The order-N operation above figure-detection: treat the whole set of detected displacements as a FIELD and find the single intended TRAJECTORY they are collectively a measurement of. It produces the RELATIONS among figures (alignment, composition, principal axis + counter-current) that a flat list cannot — the opposition between threads IS the passage argument.

attrs.name: trajectory_reading
attrs.description: The output of analysis: one Reading node = the intended trajectory of the whole passage, with accounts_for edges back to every figure it explains, a coherence score (how tightly the displacements align) and a tension score (magnitude of the surviving opposition).

attrs.name: analysis_accounts_for_all
attrs.head: good analysis
attrs.body: a good analysis explains ALL the figures, not a convenient subset; an orphan displacement is evidence the reading is wrong

attrs.name: analysis_stable_under_discount
attrs.head: good analysis
attrs.body: re-weighting figures by suspect-witness trust must not flip the trajectory; if it does, the reading rested on a discredited witness

attrs.name: analysis_is_predictive
attrs.head: good analysis
attrs.body: a newly detected figure in the same passage should resolve CONSISTENTLY with the trajectory, not against it

attrs.name: analysis_is_falsifiable
attrs.head: good analysis
attrs.body: a competing trajectory Reading must score measurably lower coherence over the same figure-set
